cards.explanation: The answer is that Tyre gloats and expects to gain. Tyre looks at Jerusalem in ruins and says, “Aha!” That is not a sympathy card, friends. The city says, “now that she lies in ruins I will be filled…” (Ezekiel 26:2). I think Tyre sees a door swinging open for itself.

The answer is False. God doesn't take Tyre's side. He says, “Behold, O Tyre, I am against you…” (Ezekiel 26:3). Then He says He will raise up many nations against her. First Tyre says “Aha!” and then God says He is against her.

The answer is destroy. God says, “They will destroy the walls of Tyre and demolish her towers.” (Ezekiel 26:4). The walls and the towers both get the same treatment. Waves don't ask permission, and neither do these nations.

The answer is nets. God says, “She will become a place to spread nets in the sea…” (Ezekiel 26:5). Once the soil is scraped off and only bare rock is left, there's room for something humble. A city with proud towers ends up as a spot to spread nets.

The answer is that they will know He is the LORD. God says, “Then they will know that I am the LORD.” (Ezekiel 26:6). After all of this, the point is who God is. It isn't a lesson about Tyre's résumé. It's about Him.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. God says, “Behold, I will bring against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings…” (Ezekiel 26:7). The name is right there in the verse. God says He is the One bringing him.

The answer is battering rams. God says, “He will direct the blows of his battering rams against your walls…” (Ezekiel 26:9). Rams, plural, so he isn't knocking politely. The verse before it has him build a ramp to her walls and raise his shields, and the rams are what he aims at those walls.
The answer is True. God says, “…your walls will shake from the noise of cavalry, wagons, and chariots.” (Ezekiel 26:10). The walls shake from the noise. That's a LOUD army, friends.
The answer is False. The pillars don't stay up. God says, “…your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.” (Ezekiel 26:11). Mighty or not, they go down.

The answer is into the water. God says they will “…throw your stones and timber and soil into the water.” (Ezekiel 26:12). Tyre sits in the sea, so I think the water is right there waiting. In the same verse He says they will demolish her walls and tear down her beautiful homes.

The answer is silenced. God says, “So I will silence the sound of your songs, and the music of your lyres will no longer be heard.” (Ezekiel 26:13). A lyre is a stringed instrument, and its music stops. A city that was full of music goes quiet.
The answer is False. God says it plainly: “You will never be rebuilt…” (Ezekiel 26:14). He repeats that she will be a bare rock and a place to spread the fishing nets. No rebuilding is promised.

The answer is that they come down from their thrones. God says, “All the princes of the sea will descend from their thrones, remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments.” (Ezekiel 26:16). Those are people used to sitting high, and now they come down. I think news like this would shake anybody's sense of being in charge.
The answer is trembling. God says they will sit on the ground, “…trembling every moment, appalled over you.” (Ezekiel 26:16). They are clothed with terror. Even with robes off, they are shaking.

The answer is her power on the sea. In their lament they call her “…she who was powerful on the sea…” (Ezekiel 26:17). They also call her a “…city of renown inhabited by seafaring men…” Tyre's strength was out on the water.
The answer is False. The lament doesn't say peace. It says Tyre was “…powerful on the sea, along with her people, who imposed terror on all peoples!” (Ezekiel 26:17). Terror is the word they use.

The answer is the deep. God says, “…when I raise up the deep against you so that the mighty waters cover you…” (Ezekiel 26:19). Tyre sits in the sea, so the waters come right to her door. The city described as powerful on the sea gets covered by the mighty waters.

The answer is False. God says He will bring her down “…so that you will no longer be inhabited or set in splendor in the land of the living.” (Ezekiel 26:20). She will no longer be inhabited. She will no longer be set in splendor either.
The answer is that she will never be found. God says, “You will be sought, but will never be found…” (Ezekiel 26:21). That is a heavy word, friends. God declares that Tyre will be no more.
